sources.title: Novva Data Centers: Las Vegas Colocation Data Center page (version modified 31 August 2026)
sources.summary: Novva's Las Vegas page calls the facility 'Novva’s newest purpose-built, future-proof data center' in Las Vegas, a 275,000 sq ft, 100 MW data center, and says 'Now accepting reservations'. Under 'Water Use, Measured and Accounted For' it states 'Our Las Vegas facility runs on ambient air cooling and waterless cooling technology' and 'We built this facility to operate differently, and we track that difference closely', publishes 2025 monthly water consumption reports (two bills per month, January to December 2025) and says the data center 'uses an average monthly water volume equivalent to roughly five typical Las Vegas households', the water serving on-site staff, landscaping and humidification. Its specifications list a 16-acre campus with 275,000 sq ft of data center space (land area 20 acres; a single-storey concrete tilt-up building of 246,328 sq ft), an on-campus 100 MW owner substation, UPS blocks with a full build of six blocks, generators, a 1.3 annualized PUE, 'On-site 24x7 staffing', a 100% uptime SLA, 24/7 security with drone surveillance and SOC 1, SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, ISO 22301 and PCI DSS attestations, and it invites visitors to tour the campus. The measured and published water use of the facility, its on-site round-the-clock staffing and the built-facility statements describe a data center in service; the reservation offer concerns available capacity.
